 THIS CCC IS FILED UNDER SECTIONS 11 AND 12 OF THE CONTEMPT OF COURTS ACT, R/W ARTICLE 215 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO INITIATE CONTEMPT PROCEEDINGS AND PUNISH THE RESPONDENTS/ACCUSED UNDER THE CONTEMPT ACT FOR NOT COMPLYING THE ORDER DATED 26.11.2021 IN WRIT PETITION NO. 205306 OF 2019 VIDE ANNEXURE-A.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, B.M. SHYAM PRASAD, J., MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners were the owners of certain extents of lands in Survey Nos.29, 23/2, 23/6B, 23/4B and 36/5 of NC: 2023:KHC-K:1105-DB Biddapur Village, Kalaburagi Taluk and District and their writ petition in WP No.205306/2019 is disposed of on 26.11.2021 with directions that read hereunder:

"The respondents are directed to consider the representations of the petitioners at Annexures - F, F1, F2, G, G1 and G2 to the writ petition as expeditiously as possible,
complete the acquisition proceedings and award compensation to the petitioners in accordance with law, not later than one year from today."
The fourth respondent viz., the concerned Executive Engineer is appointed as the Litigation Conducting Officer, and on his behalf a memo is placed enclosing certain documents.

2. Sri Shivakumar Tengli, the learned counsel for the respondents, relying upon the documents as aforesaid, submits that upon due service of notice it is ascertained that certain extents in about 11 survey numbers of this village, including the complainants' lands, have been utilized without acquisition and NC: 2023:KHC-K:1105-DB therefore, a proposal, in the prescribed form is sent for a minimum deposit of Rs.1.00 crore and for issuance of notification in law for payment of compensation.

sentences.text: When queried, Sri Shivakumar Tengli submits that the proposal is sent to the office of the Deputy Commissioner, who will have to forward the proposal to the concerned SLAO for initiation of appropriate proceedings, and he further submits, on instructions from the fourth respondent, that this would be done within a period of 4 [four] months.

There is delay in commencing the proceedings to ascertain whether the complainants' lands are utilized without acquisition and in commencing the appropriate proceedings, but reasons are offered stating that the delay is not intentional.

4. On careful consideration of the circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that the contempt proceedings must be dropped accepting the reasons offered to explain the delay but with liberty to the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1105-DB complainants to take appropriate action in the event the proposal now made does not fructify into an effective action within 4 [four] months as now stated.
The contempt proceedings stand dropped subject to the above.
